disclaimer: General bargain tips from public shopping knowledge and open consumer guidance — not scraped from proprietary store apps. Always verify prices and store policies locally.

tips.title: Compare unit price, not just shelf price
tips.body: Look at price per ounce, pound, or sheet. Warehouse packs and dollar-store sizes can look cheap until you normalize.

tips.title: WinCo for staples; Grocery Outlet for surprises
tips.body: In Redding, many shoppers use WinCo for milk, eggs, rice, and produce staples, then hit Grocery Outlet for rotating closeouts (coffee, snacks, sauces).

tips.title: Drugstore ads need coupons
tips.body: CVS and Walgreens weekly ads often assume ExtraCare / myWalgreens digital coupons. Shelf price alone can look high — check the ad + app before buying HBA.

tips.title: Costco when the unit math wins
tips.body: Membership cost spreads across big trips. Best for chicken packs, toilet paper, butter, and rice if you have storage and will use it before spoilage.

tips.title: Safeway / Raley's for sale weeks + rewards
tips.body: Mid-tier grocers shine when the weekly ad hits your list. Stack store digital coupons with advertised sales when the store allows it.

tips.title: SNAP / EBT awareness
tips.body: Many Redding grocery locations accept SNAP/EBT for eligible foods. Hot prepared foods and most non-food HBA are usually excluded — confirm at checkout.

tips.title: Plan by store, not by aisle alone
tips.body: Split the list: staples at a budget grocer, sale meat/produce at whoever is cheapest that week, HBA where the coupon math works.

tips.title: Open sources for circulars
tips.body: Prefer retailer weekly-ad web pages you are allowed to view, or manually typed CSV updates. Do not scrape Instacart, GasBuddy, or proprietary apps that forbid it.
